guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 authorization code flow with PKCE for user-consented access. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts as the user across the API, and the app must enforce read-only use itself.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider with authorization code grant and PKCE
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider with user consent. Its documented grant is Authorization Code, with PKCE and OpenID Connect extensions. Confidential and public client types are supported.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer connects an individual account on its own Forgejo instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: OAuth2 tokens have no scope boundary and act as the user
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented. OAuth tokens can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. Third-party applications that obtain a token through this provider have administrative rights.
findings.appliesWhen: The app uses OAuth2 tokens for the connected customer.

evidence.quote: Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.
Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Register the OAuth application in the instance user settings
findings.detail: Any user can register an OAuth2 application on the applications settings page. The redirect URI must match the authorize and token requests. Client ID and secret must be configured in the app.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first OAuth test on each customer instance.

evidence.quote: It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

findings.title: The instance API must be enabled and the search endpoint must return visible repositories
findings.detail: The API is enabled by default, but instance administrators may disable it. GET /api/v1/repos/search includes private repositories the user can access by default and supports page and limit parameters.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer instance has the API enabled and the connected person can access the repositories.

evidence.quote: Enabling/configuring API access By default, the API is enabled on Forgejo instances, but instance administrators may choose to disable it .
## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true) Schema: {"type":"boolean"}

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 application as a public client
steps.detail: On the customer's Forgejo instance, the connected person creates an OAuth2 application at /user/settings/applications as a public client (PKCE, no client secret). Set one redirect URI matching the app callback. Record the Client ID. Public-client PKCE is the single first-test path.
steps.doneWhen: The application exists with a Client ID, is marked public, and its redirect URI matches the app callback exactly.

evidence.quote: Note Please ensure you have registered your OAuth application as a public client.

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

fields: Instance base URL: customer-supplied, e.g. https://forgejo.example.com
Redirect URI: app callback URL, must match exactly

steps.title: Generate PKCE code_verifier and code_challenge
steps.detail: The app generates a random code_verifier of 43 to 128 characters using alphanumerics and - . _ ~, then derives code_challenge as the URL-safe base64 SHA256 of it with code_challenge_method=S256.
steps.doneWhen: The app holds a code_verifier and matching S256 code_challenge before building the authorization URL.

steps.title: Redirect the user to the authorization endpoint and verify the callback
steps.detail: Send the connected person to the authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, code_challenge_method=S256, code_challenge and state. The person approves access in the browser. The app checks that the returned state matches and that a code is present. This step is user-performed and not executed by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect returns to the app callback with a code and the same state value.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token with PKCE
steps.detail: POST the returned code, client_id, redirect_uri, the grant_type constant authorization_code and the code_verifier to the token endpoint. Public clients send no client_secret. The response contains access_token and refresh_token. Keep the token server-side.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token and token_type bearer.

steps.title: List visible repositories, first page
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with a bearer token, page=1 and limit. Read names from $.data[].name. Show the Link and x-total-count headers with --include. Omit the sort filter to keep the documented default. Initial request for the paginated collection, paired with its continuation.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 and the first page of repository names is returned. HTTP 200 with the first page returned. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /api/v1/repos/search: $.data[].name (string)
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Follow the next page of visible repositories
steps.detail: Repeat the listing with the next page using the same parameters, resolving the next link from the prior response Link header against the instance host. Continue until no rel=next link is returned, or the x-total-count is reached. Continue with the rel=next link from the prior response. Stop when no rel=next link is returned.
steps.doneWhen: The next page returns HTTP 200 and no rel=next link remains, or total count is covered. No rel=next link remains in the Link header. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

steps.detail: Inspect the app's outgoing request log to confirm only GET requests were sent. Note that OAuth tokens have no scope boundary and act as the user, so read-only use depends on the app's own request filtering.
steps.doneWhen: The request log shows only GET calls to the listing endpoint.
